column2: What can you see in simple mode?
column3: The tree with the person in the middle, their spouse, their parents and their children, the relationship written in plain words (“your grandmother”, “the husband of your granddaughter Émilie”); the photos in large size with “🔊 Listen” and “👥 Who is there?”; a simple record whose story is written in sentences (birth, baptism, marriage, occupation, death); the people by family, by first name or by searching (big keyboard, 🎤 dictation); “On this day”: birthdays, marriages, photos of the month and what is coming soon. Living people can be shown, reduced to their first name or hidden; confidential records are never shown; removed photos and records are not shown (without being deleted).

column2: How do I simplify the screen (“one thing at a time” mode)?
column3: Settings → Accessibility → “🧩 One thing at a time”. The app hides the rarely used tools (DNA, comparison, split screen, dashboard settings, deleting or locking a record…) and enlarges the main buttons. Nothing is deleted: the “Simple mode — Show everything” banner, at the bottom right, brings everything back in one click.

column2: How do I have a screen reader read the description of images?
column3: Settings → Accessibility → “Describe the images”. Each photo in your media is read with its description, otherwise its title, its date, its place and the people linked to it. To write it yourself, open a media item: “Image description (read aloud)” field.

column2: How do I always show the subtitles of videos and montages?
column3: Settings → Accessibility → “Subtitles always shown”. Videos that have subtitles show them automatically; in the montage, the “Subtitles” track is visible during playback even if it is hidden. The exported video does not change.

column2: How do I fill in a field by speaking (voice dictation)?
column3: Settings → Accessibility → “Voice dictation”. A 🎤 appears in the field you are writing in: click it (or Ctrl + Shift + Space), speak, and the text is written at the cursor. Say “comma”, “full stop”, “new line”… for punctuation, Esc to stop. If your computer does not offer dictation here: on a Mac, the system dictation (🎤 key or Fn twice); on Windows, Windows + H.

column2: Which font should I choose to read more easily (dyslexia)?
column3: Settings → Accessibility → Text → Font. “Very legible” (Atkinson Hyperlegible) and “OpenDyslexic” are stored in the app: nothing to install, and they work without the Internet. “Comic Sans” is your computer’s font: if it is missing, the app uses OpenDyslexic instead.

column2: Can I ask a question with a precise date?
column3: Yes: “Who was born on 7 May 1950?”, “born in May 1950”, “born on 15 Brumaire Year II”, “born in Year II”, “died aged 70”, “died before age 5”. If the date does not exist, the app tells you instead of listing everything.

column2: How does the question in plain language know who I am talking about?
column3: “How many ancestors does Jean Martin have?” counts those of Jean Martin; without a name, it is the starting person, and the app says so. A first name alone is enough if it is unique; otherwise the app shows you the records to choose from.

column2: Can I ask for cousins, half-brothers or inconsistent dates?
column3: “The first cousins of Louis Martin”, “the half-sisters of…”; “brothers and sisters” separates those who have the same parents from the half-siblings. “Who died before being born?” or “inconsistent dates” lists the dates to check. Animals are not counted among the people; ask “who are the animals”.

column2: What does “pedigree collapse” mean in the Sosa list?
column3: An ancestor who appears at several Sosa numbers (for example cousins who married each other): this is normal, it is not a duplicate to merge.

column2: Why does the Date box accept 29 February 1500?
column3: Before 1583, the Julian calendar was used, in which every year divisible by 4 has a 29 February. Years before 1000 are understood, but the app does not sort them yet (yellow warning).

column2: What happens when I remove a parent?
column3: The other parent remains the child’s parent. If you put the parent back afterwards, the child returns to the couple.

column2: How are half-brothers and half-sisters arranged?
column3: If someone had several spouses, a child added is no longer automatically put with one of them: add the 2nd parent and the child joins the right couple. A child never has three parents.

column2: Why can’t I remove a spouse?
column3: A couple who have a marriage, sources, notes, media or children together cannot be separated with one click: the message says what to remove first.

column2: What does the lock on a record block?
column3: A locked record no longer changes at all: events, sources, photos, labels, name variants, hypotheses, family links, notes. Unlock it to edit it.

column2: Why is the merge refused?
column3: You cannot merge two spouses, nor an ancestor with their descendant: they are not the same person.

column2: Do I need to type accents to search?
column3: No: “helene” finds Hélène, “jean-baptiste” finds Jean Baptiste. The quick search also looks in the other names of a record (variants).

column2: Why does Lists → Places show fewer places?
column3: The list only shows the places of your genealogy (and those you created), not the 80,000 reference communes. Lists → People does not show animals, and a marriage shows both spouses.

column2: What does a GEDCOM export keep?
column3: Labels, animals, note titles and dates in the Republican or Julian calendar are kept, and the import reads them back. An impossible link (someone who would be their own ancestor) is ignored on import and reported.

column2: How are Republican and very old dates sorted?
column3: A Republican date (“15 Brumaire Year II”) gets its Gregorian equivalent and its year, for sorting and ages. Years before 1000 are understood (“about 845”).

column2: Why does the button show “Saving…”?
column3: While saving, the button waits: a double-click or a repeated Enter no longer creates a duplicate. It goes back to normal as soon as it is finished, even if there is an error.

column2: What does the Enter key do in a window?
column3: In a one-line box, Enter saves the window (like the blue button); it no longer closes it and loses what was typed. In a large text, Enter goes to a new line.

column2: What does “changed in another window” mean?
column3: If the same record, the same board or the same layout is open in two tabs, LCNDA no longer silently replaces what the other one saved: reload to see the other version, or choose “Save anyway” / “Keep my version”.

column2: What if LCNDA stops responding?
column3: The message “No connection with LCNDA” says so, what you typed stays in the window and “Try again” restarts the saving. If you close or reload the tab with unsaved input, the browser asks first.

column2: How does Esc work?
column3: Esc closes windows and tools (drawing, house…) when nothing is in progress. If there are changes, it asks first, and pressing several times no longer makes you lose anything. In a search box, Esc empties it first.

column2: What does ⌘Z (Ctrl+Z) do outside the editors?
column3: It immediately undoes the last record created (if nothing has been added to it), a lock or a family link, with “↷ Redo”. Otherwise it explains how to undo by hand.

column2: What happens to the witnesses and godparents of a deleted record?
column3: Deleting a record or an event also removes its witnesses and godparents; restoring puts them back.

column2: How do I reopen an exported slideshow?
column3: A file exported with “⤓ Export → 💾 File” is reopened with “⤒ Import a slideshow” in the list of slideshows.

column2: How do I zoom on a phone?
column3: In the house, the drawing and the presentation, two fingers zoom the plan or the slide, not the page.

column2: Can I get back a widget removed from the dashboard?
column3: Yes: “↶ Undo” in the message at the bottom left. An empty dashboard offers “＋ Add a widget”.

column2: What is the bar above the lists for?
column3: All lists now have the same bar, always in this order: 🔍 Search (“/” key to go there, Esc or × to empty it), “Filter ▾”, “List | Cards” and “Sort”. In “Filter ▾”, each section shows its choices with their number (Kind, State, Place 📍, Person 👤, Label 🏷, Period…); the chosen filters appear under the bar as blue badges (“Women ×”): a click on a badge removes it, “Clear all” removes them all. “Sort” always starts with “Newest, Oldest, A → Z, Z → A”, then the list’s own sorts; clicking a column heading also sorts. Each list remembers your settings, even after closing the app. A list that is still empty shows no bar, only the button to get started. The Treasures (Letters, Candles, Shares, Places passport, Missing records, Gazettes) also have the bar: “Lit” or “In progress” is the starting choice, as a badge (× to see everything); a sealed letter is never searched in its text. The two calendars (My diary, Family calendar) only have 🔍 and “Filter ▾” (Kind, Person, Place): the search works in all views. In “My lists”: “List | Cards” and “More ▾” for the other layouts (by group, draggable columns, timeline, gallery), “Filter ▾” has a section per column (the ▾ of a column heading opens it) and these filters are stored in the list; “⤓ Export ▾” and “🖨 Print” are at the top, Edit, Duplicate and Delete in “⋯”.

column2: Why doesn’t the app ask me “Are you sure?” before deleting any more?
column3: For a note, an event, a row, an item in a tool…, the deletion happens straight away and a message at the bottom left offers “↶ Undo” for 6 seconds (hovering over it pauses the time). After Undo, “↷ Redo” does the deletion again. The question remains only for what cannot be recovered: a whole record, a database, emptying the bin.

column2: Are the CSV files I download safe?
column3: Yes: a text beginning with =, +, - or @ is preceded by an apostrophe, so that Excel, Numbers or LibreOffice do not take it for a hidden formula.

column2: How do I visit my house as if I were there?
column3: House → 3D view → “🚶 Visit”. Walk with W A S D or the arrows, Shift to run. Click the view to look around with the mouse, Esc to release it, Esc again to leave. You go through doors, not through walls. On a staircase: E to go up, C to go down (or the ⬆ ⬇ buttons). The small map shows where you are; a click on it takes you there. The eye height can be set (1.60 m, or 1 m to see like a child). On a tablet, walk with the circle at the bottom left.

column2: How do I see the sunlight in my house?
column3: 3D view → “☀️ Light”. Choose the time and the day (Winter, Summer…), or “▶ See the day”. The sun is calculated for the location of the house (otherwise the centre of France). Set “North of the plan” if the top of your plan does not face north. At night, the lamps, chandeliers and candles placed light up. Also in the House tab → “☀️ Orientation and light”.

column2: How do I trace my house over the Napoleonic cadastre?
column3: ⤒ Import → “📐 An old plan, a cadastre” (or Floor tab → Old plan): choose the image in the media or import it. Click both ends of a known length and give its real length (metres, toises, French feet…). “↻ Straighten” makes a wall straight in two clicks. Set the transparency, lock, then “✏️ Trace the walls” and draw over it.
